title: CS1-WINDOW-P-MIN-E with stacked envelopes and heralded fraction 1-1/(10^64-3)^4

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N) and P=u_333, where u_333 is the exact Pell numerator in proof.md Section 0. The CS1-WINDOW-P-MIN-E algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 from independent ideal coset copies. Its total charged work on every execution branch is O(n^20 2^(c sqrt(n))), where c=sqrt(2+4/P^2). With the exact Pell rational a and E defined in proof.md Section 14, this is O(E(n)); the complete supported expression E is the structured time bound. This same configuration and success guarantee establish all other resource and tolerance claims jointly. The exact time-envelope growth index is 1/2. The same bound also holds on every branch under the heralded-erasure model and fractional promise of claim 4, counting all raw acquisitions, because the filter overhead is an absolute constant.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N), P=u_333, where u_333 is the exact Pell numerator in proof.md Section 0, c=sqrt(2+4/P^2), and beta=c-sqrt(2)/P. The same CS1-WINDOW-P-MIN-E algorithm and parameters in proof.md use at most O(n^20 2^(beta sqrt(n))) classical bits on every execution branch. With the exact rational , proved in Section 14 to exceed beta, this is O(E_b(n)), where E_b(n) = 2^(b sqrt(n) - sum_(i=1..28) k_i n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(10^256 - i))) with k_1 = ... = k_27 = 10^256 - 1 and k_28 = 10^58 - 1 (envelopes.md Lemma E2, using only b - beta > 0; the structured object lists E_b term by term). All bounds, the heralded-erasure guarantee and clean-input guarantee and recovery probability at least 1-2^-8 hold jointly for this configuration. The exact growth index of the declared envelope is 1/2. The same bound also holds on every branch under the heralded-erasure model and fractional promise of claim 4, counting all raw acquisitions, because the filter overhead is an absolute constant.

The same CS1-WINDOW-P-MIN-E configuration, with the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md Section 11.1 (literal raw-acquisition cutoff D Qcap*, with D = m^4 and Qcap* = Qcap on the main branch, N(n+10) on the finite branch), proves fractional error tolerance epsilon(n) = 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999996*9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999998*5909009547859618446014307935656485996455360061473289284034355157*8461654968574415353741992088106541809421651544931744139485636465*2/9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999997^4 = 1 - 1/m^4, a constant in (0,1), where m and the factors are the integers of proof.md Section 15 (m = x = 10^64 - 3; the displayed integers t_i of Section 15 multiply to x^2 + 1, so the expression is (x^4 - 1)/x^4). Under the stated heralded malformed-copy model, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), if at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed on every branch, the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3, and the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 hold jointly on every execution branch in the form stated there for the heralded model. With no malformed copies (the clean problem, no herald) the algorithm is the clean algorithm. No positive tolerance is claimed for undetectable corruptions.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
